description:
Eye from Above — Satellite-Powered Disaster Intelligence

When disasters strike, relief teams struggle to identify affected areas. Eye from Above uses NASA's NISAR radar data to detect surface changes and generate disaster impact maps, highlighting affected zones and infrastructure at risk. By combining SAR analysis with geographic data, it helps relief teams prioritize areas and assess potential access routes, turning satellite observations into actionable insights for disaster response.
summary: Eye from Above is an AI-powered disaster response web platform and interactive decision-support dashboard built using NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) L-Band observations for the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge. During catastrophic monsoon floods, thick storm clouds blind optical satellites for days while raw SAR backscatter data is too complex for field responders to interpret. Our platform converts multi-temporal NISAR L-band imagery into plain-English, life-saving intelligence: (1) cloud-penetrating flood maps separating shallow water from deep boat-only channels, (2) population-ranked trapped village priorities, (3) AI-scored rescue base selection and verified dry truck corridors, (4) predictive flood-surge simulations (+0m to +300m) with automatic boat drop-off relocation, (5) 72-hour Sphere humanitarian supply calculations, and (6) zero-internet offline responder kits.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS:

Eye from Above transforms all-weather NASA NISAR L-Band (~24 cm wavelength) radar backscatter data into an operational flood rescue command system, validated on the August 2026 monsoon flood in the Koshi River Basin (Saptari District, Nepal).

1. All-Weather SAR Physics & Flood Segmentation (analyze_disaster.py): Unlike optical cameras blocked by storm clouds, NISAR's active L-band radar penetrates monsoon clouds and crop canopies. Smooth standing floodwater causes specular mirror reflection (backscatter < -17.5 dB, appearing jet-black), while rough dry terrain scatters energy back (bright gray). Comparing pre-flood baseline scans (Aug 19, 2026) with peak flood scans (Aug 31, 2026) isolates 35.86 km² of active inundation and separates shallow floodwater from deep boat-only channels (< -19.5 dB) in metric UTM Zone 45N (EPSG:32645).

2. Priority Village Exposure Ranking (fix_zones.py): Fuses NISAR flood polygons with OpenStreetMap building footprints within a 500 m buffer to deduplicate and rank the top 5 trapped villages by exposed population (led by Gobargadha Island with ~3,992 people and Tilathi Koiladi with ~4,768 people).

3. MCDA AI Rescue Base Scoring & Safe Dry Routing (app.py): Prunes 24 submerged road segments from the road graph and evaluates 5 rescue bases out of 100 using weighted Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (45% dry road speed via Dijkstra routing, 35% medical/boat capacity, 20% route flood safety). It routes trucks from the top-ranked base (Central Koshi High-Ground Medical Post, Score: 86.8/100) along a 7.73 km (~13 min) verified dry road to the exact Boat Drop-Off point (26.3515° N, 86.6565° E).

4. Predictive Flood Surge Simulator (+0m to +300m): Simulates radial water expansion. When water rises >= +100m (expanding flooding to 326.88 km² and blocking 100 road sections at +250m), the system detects that the boat launch point is submerged and automatically relocates it to higher dry ground (26.3645° N, 86.6490° E; 6.24 km / ~10 min drive).

5. 72-Hour Sphere Supply Calculator & Offline Field Kit: Computes 3-day water (3 L/person/day), ready meals, tents, boats, and trucks per Sphere standards, and exports standalone offline .html maps, .geojson GPS tracks, and .md mission sheets.

TOOLS & CODING LANGUAGES USED:

Python 3.10+, Streamlit, GeoPandas, Rasterio, OSMnx, NetworkX, Folium, Shapely, NumPy, PyProj, Matplotlib, HTML5, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript (ES6+), and Leaflet.js.

Source Code Repository: https://github.com/ahmedsaberasa/eye-from-above

SAMPLE TASK FOR JUDGES TO TRY:

Open our Live Streamlit App (https://eye-from-above-cky3vjkcrdmbcbzdlws3uh.streamlit.app/), select any of the 5 trapped villages in the sidebar, drag the Flood Expansion Simulator slider from +0m to +250m to watch the Boat Drop-Off point relocate automatically, inspect Before/After radar scans, and download the offline field files. You can also explore our 7-slide interactive demo at https://ahmedsaberasa.github.io/eye-from-above/.

WHAT WORKS NOW, CURRENT LIMITATIONS & FUTURE PLANS:

- What Works Now: Full interactive Streamlit dashboard, 7-slide live satellite presentation, MCDA base ranking, Dijkstra dry road routing, +0m to +300m surge simulation, Sphere supply math, and offline .html/.geojson/.md exports.

- Current Limitations: Raw multi-temporal SAR GeoTIFFs exceed GitHub's 25 MB web upload limit, so our public repo stores pre-extracted vector flood polygons (GeoJSON) and pruned road graphs (GraphML); the surge simulator uses planar metric buffering in EPSG:32645 rather than a 3D hydrodynamic solver; population counts rely on static OSM building footprints.

- Future Plans: Direct NASA Earthdata / ASF Vertex cloud API streaming for real-time global NISAR scenes, integration of NASA SRTM 30m DEM elevation contours, and two-way SMS / LoRa mesh updates from field rescue boats.
